findings.evidence: Mathlib/Probability/StrongLaw.lean:787 `theorem strong_law_ae (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (hint : Integrable (X 0) μ) ...` — integrability, no boundedness. In the proof here, `hbdd` occurs only at lines 113 and 120.
findings.fix: Replace `{C : ℝ} (hbdd : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C)` by `(hint : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Integrable f (ν ω))` in both theorems. Transfer it to `∀ᵐ Q ∂(μ.map ν), Integrable f Q` with `ae_map_iff`, using that `{Q | Integrable f Q} = {Q | ∫⁻ y, ‖f y‖₊ ∂Q < ∞}` is measurable by `Measure.measurable_lintegral`, and replace `simp [hfibre]` with an a.e.-vanishing integrand. The indicator corollaries (lines 167, 185) discharge the new hypothesis in one step.
findings.issue: `ConditionallyIIDWith.tendsto_average_ae` assumes `{C : ℝ} (hbdd : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C)`. Boundedness is strictly stronger than the standard hypothesis for a strong law and is not what the proof needs: the bound is used only (i) to get `Integrable f Q` on each fibre — required only for `μ.map ν`-a.e. `Q`, since `Measure.bind_apply` integrates the fibrewise null sets — and (ii) to feed `measurable_probabilityMeasure_integral`. The bounded statement gives no route to the unbounded one, so the conditional SLLN for e.g. an integrable-but-unbounded observable is unreachable from this API. Same assumption at line 151 (`tendsto_integral_empiricalMeasure_ae`).

findings.evidence: The repo already uses exactly this derivation pattern: TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasureExt.lean:82-84 `measurable_probabilityMeasure_toMeasure_apply … := (Measure.measurable_coe hs).comp measurable_subtype_coe`. Mathlib's Giry-level companion `Measure.measurable_lintegral` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/GiryMonad.lean:116) has no side condition beyond `Measurable f`.
findings.fix: Prove `Measurable fun μ : Measure α => ∫ y, f y ∂μ` for measurable `f`, with the integrability set as a `Set.indicator`/`Measurable.ite`, and derive the `ProbabilityMeasure` form as `(…).comp measurable_subtype_coe`. This also supplies the measurability step the generalization in finding 1 needs.
findings.issue: `measurable_probabilityMeasure_integral` is stated at two levels below the natural one. The bound `∀ x, |f x| ≤ C` serves only to produce `Integrable f P` (line 55), and the restriction to `ProbabilityMeasure α` is undone inside the proof by `measurable_subtype_coe`. For a measurable `f : α → ℝ`, `fun μ : Measure α => ∫ y, f y ∂μ` is measurable outright: `{μ | ∫⁻ y, ‖f y‖₊ ∂μ < ∞}` is measurable by `Measure.measurable_lintegral`, off it the integral is the junk value `0` (`integral_undef`), and on it the two-halves decomposition already used applies.

findings.fix: Drop `hf`: run the argument for `g := hint.1.mk f` (`StronglyMeasurable`, hence `Measurable` under the ambient `[BorelSpace E]`), then transfer back — `f (x i) = g (x i)` holds `P`-a.e. for each `i` because `measurePreserving_eval_infinitePi` (already used at line 78) pushes the `Q`-null set forward, and the countable union over `i` is null; `∫ f dQ = ∫ g dQ` by `integral_congr_ae`.
findings.issue: `strong_law_ae_infinitePi` takes `hf : Measurable f` alongside `hint : Integrable f Q`. Measurability is stronger than the Bochner-API convention (`AEStronglyMeasurable`, already contained in `hint.1`), and Mathlib's `strong_law_ae` imposes no measurability hypothesis at all; `hf` is used only for `IndepFun.comp` at line 86.

summary: The headline conditional strong law is stated for bounded observables where the standard hypothesis (and Mathlib's own `strong_law_ae`) is integrability, and the bounded case cannot be used to recover the general one; the supporting measurability lemma carries the same avoidable bound and sits at `ProbabilityMeasure` rather than the Giry-level `Measure α`.
